title: Career roadmap · Inventory Planner
summary: An Inventory Planner balances stock availability, demand, purchasing, replenishment and inventory costs so that a business can meet customer demand without carrying unnecessary inventory.

facts.Timeline assumption: This roadmap assumes a standard 3-year BBA. If a 4-year honours/research variant is available, use the additional year for advanced demand planning, supply-chain analytics, ERP systems, internships and a major inventory-planning project.

about.label: Course alignment
about.text: Inventory Planner is directly aligned with the BBA – Logistics & Supply Chain pathway.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Build inventory, procurement, logistics, Excel, forecasting and supply-chain fundamentals; gain warehouse/planning exposure through internships.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Specialise in demand planning, replenishment, supply planning, procurement analytics, warehouse planning or supply-chain analytics.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Progress toward Senior Inventory Planner, Demand Planner, Supply Planner, Inventory Manager or Supply Chain Analyst.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Combine supply-chain strategy, advanced forecasting, AI-assisted planning, ERP systems, analytics and working-capital management.

Career progression
Alternative route:
Progression depends on planning responsibility, industry, ERP expertise and measurable improvements in inventory/service levels.
PhD routes
Potential research areas include:
A PhD is mainly relevant to research, teaching, advanced optimisation or specialised supply-chain research.

The long-term goal should be to move from inventory monitoring to end-to-end planning leadership. AI and advanced forecasting will automate more routine replenishment and prediction, so senior professionals should develop expertise in scenario planning, supply risk, working capital, supplier strategy, network optimisation and cross-functional decision-making.
